hash.description: Turn text into a fixed-length fingerprint with SHA-256, SHA-512, MD5 or another hash. The same text always gives the same hash and nothing can be read back from it, so it works for checksums, spotting duplicates, and comparing values without storing them.
hash.name: hash

parameters.description: The hash to use. SHA-256 is what nearly every API asks for; MD5 and SHA-1 suit checksums and older services but are not safe against tampering.
parameters.name: algorithm

parameters.description: How the hash is written: hexadecimal (the usual form), Base64, or URL-safe Base64 without padding.
parameters.name: encoding

returns.description: The hash, written in the chosen encoding: 64 hexadecimal characters for SHA-256.

hmac.description: Compute an HMAC: a hash of the text keyed with a shared secret, the way webhooks and API requests are signed. Only someone who knows the secret can produce it, so use it to sign what you send, or recompute it to check a signature you received.
hmac.name: hmac

parameters.description: The text to sign, such as a request body.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The shared secret. Write @secrets.NAME to use a workspace secret rather than pasting it here.
parameters.name: secret

parameters.description: The hash the HMAC is built on. Most services use SHA-256; a few older ones use SHA-1.
parameters.name: algorithm

parameters.description: How the HMAC is written: hexadecimal (the usual form), Base64, or URL-safe Base64 without padding. Match what the service you are talking to expects.
parameters.name: encoding

returns.description: The HMAC, written in the chosen encoding: 64 hexadecimal characters for SHA-256.

random_secret.description: Make a random string from a secure source of randomness, for an API key, a password, a signing secret, a one-time code or a token to put in a link.
random_secret.name: random_secret

parameters.description: How many characters, 1 to 1024. 32 hexadecimal characters hold 128 bits of randomness, plenty for an API key; a one-time code is usually 6 digits.
parameters.name: length

parameters.description: What the secret is made of.
parameters.name: format

returns.description: A random string of the chosen length and characters, different every time.

sign.description: Create a digital signature for text with an RSA, EC (ECDSA) or Ed25519 private key, as a JWT, a Google service account or a signed URL needs. Anyone with the matching public key can check the signature; only the private key can make it.
sign.display_name: Sign text with a private key
sign.name: sign

parameters.description: The private key in PEM form, from -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- to -----END PRIVATE KEY-----, without a passphrase. Write @secrets.NAME to use a workspace secret rather than pasting it here.
parameters.name: private_key

parameters.description: The hash the signature is built on. An RSA key signs with PKCS#1 v1.5 (RS256 for SHA-256), an EC key with ECDSA (ES256), written the way OpenSSL writes it, or the way a JWT carries it when the text is a JWT's header and claims; an Ed25519 key ignores this choice.
parameters.name: algorithm

parameters.description: How the signature is written: Base64 (the usual form), URL-safe Base64 without padding (what a JWT needs), or hexadecimal.
parameters.name: encoding

options.label: Base64, URL-safe (no padding, for a JWT)

returns.description: The signature, written in the chosen encoding. Its length follows the key: 344 Base64 characters for a 2048-bit RSA key, 86 for Ed25519.

description: Hash text, sign it with a secret or a private key, and generate random secrets.
